newsitem.title: ITALY: Cargo plane crashes in Italian village, 5 dead.
newsitem.headline: Cargo plane crashes in Italian village, 5 dead.

text.p: An Antonov cargo plane crashed into an Italian village while attempting to land at Turin airport on Tuesday, killing at least five people, officials said.
"I heard a dull thud, I went out and I saw the tail of the plane sticking out of a house," said Alessandro Renzi, who lives close to the scene of the accident.
"Then I saw two men come out of the plane's tail and walk towards me in a confused state asking me in English to call an ambulance," Renzi told Reuters.
Rescue workers said 20 people were injured in the crash in the village of San Francesco al Campo as the jet-powered Antonov 124 came in to land on a flight from Moscow.
Those killed included the pilot, two crew members and at least two people on the ground, an official of the local prefecture said.
Another three villagers were feared dead, buried in rubble as the plane ploughed through buildings before coming to rest less than a km ( half a mile) from Turin's Caselle airport.

The plane was owned by the Moscow-based Ayaks Cargo Airlines, a company spokesman in Britain said. It was leased to the Russian airline Aeroflot, which provided the crew, and chartered by the British air cargo broker Aviation Consultants, the spoesman said.
It appeared to have aborted a first attempt to land but stalled as it circled for a fresh approach to the runway, the prefecture official said.

The plane was to have picked up a consignment of luxury vehicles, believed to have been Ferrari sports cars, before flying to the Gulf state of Sharjah and on to Brunei in the Far East. The cause of the crash was not immediately clear.
Initial reports said 22 people had been killed in the crash.
The plane struck two houses before smashing into a farm building and coming to a halt on a road close to a cemetery in the village of San Francesco del Campo.
Firemen said later they feared the plane, which still had a large amount of fuel in its tanks, might blow up.
Italian television showed images of the mangled wreckage of the plane covered in rubble. Splintered pieces of the plane's undercarriage were seen lodged in a nearby barn.
Rescue officials said there were believed to have been 24 people on board the aircraft. Other reports put the number of people at 20 to 23.
